transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Kendra Moss (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (CobaltRetail Head of ML), Marcus Li (Infra), Ellen Rivera (Product), Jon Park (SRE)

SUMMARY (auto): Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning for pilot. Review of last week's load test, discussion of continuous batching and concurrency targets, queueing/redis patch behavior, and next steps for a longer stress run. Agreed to try a 2-hour run with adjusted batching, share logs, and reconvene.

TOPICS: throughput numbers, continuous batching config, concurrency targets, queue depth, tail latency (p95/p99), KV cache warmup, fallback routing, dedicated vs hosted considerations, cost delta estimate

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. Quick check — is everyone on for the throughput hangout?
[00:12] Priya: Yep, we're good. Hoping to get clarification on the weird p99 spikes we saw last Friday.
[00:18] Daniel: Cool. We'll walk through the test artifacts we ran overnight and the tuning knobs we changed, notably continuous batching window, max concurrency, and queue depth.
[00:28] Marcus: Quick heads-up — the test load we sent had a bimodal request size distribution, small chat-ish requests and longer seq gen for product descriptions.
[00:40] Kendra: Noted — that mixed profile is what we expected given the pilot traffic, thanks Marcus.
[00:45] [00:45] Priya: Ok, show us the numbers.
[00:48] Daniel: Alright, slide one — the 1-hour run at concurrency 24 with batch max 32 gave us effective throughput ~1.8k tok/s aggregated across two GPUs. p95 stayed ~120ms but p99 had spikes 700–1,200ms.
[01:08] Ellen: Those p99 spikes are what killed our SLA headroom last week.
[01:12] Daniel: Right. We instrumented and saw the majority of p99s align with warm KV cache misses and occasional large batches that pushed serialization overhead on the CPU side.
[01:24] Priya: When you say warm misses, are we talking cold KV cache after scale events or per-request cache invalidation?
[01:30] Daniel: Mostly cold after autoscaler scaled up; the KV cache is per-GPU and the cache warming time depends on prefix reuse. We also saw queueing backpressure — some requests timed out at the ingress layer and retried, creating bursts.
[01:44] Marcus: Our autoscaler currently adds pods in 60s intervals, which probably exacerbates the cold-starts.
[01:50] Daniel: Yeah, and the current cluster autoscaler tend to create new nodes that take a few minutes to join in. For that reason we recommended pinning a minimum of reserved capacity during the 2-hour run.
[02:00] Avery: Can you remind the group what you changed in config for the last run?
[02:05] Daniel: Sure — we set continuous_batching.window_ms to 18 (was 12), max_batch_tokens to 32k, max_concurrency_per_replica to 24 (was 16), and queue_depth to 128. Also enabled async-kv-prefetch (experimental flag) to prefetch prefix keys.
[02:28] Priya: Ok so window increased, concurrency increased. Did you see improved throughput?
[02:33] Daniel: Yes throughput improved 18% on average, GPU utilization jumped from ~62% to ~78%, but the p99 tail still had outliers tied to cold KV and occasional big request serialization.
[02:48] Jon: We saw a pattern where 1 in ~200 requests was a 1.2s outlier, those matched the larger sequence length samples.
[02:57] Daniel: Correct. For those we want to consider a size-based routing rule — route long sequences to lower-concurrency dedicated lanes so they don't block the small chat requests.
[03:10] Priya: That would be ideal. We can't have product description jobs starving chat latencies.
[03:15] Avery: Tradeoff there is cost — separate lanes reduce tail coupling but increase idle cycles. We'll model that.
[03:20] [03:20] Ellen: Also curious about batching — are you seeing wasted tokens because of padding when batch shapes diverge?
[03:27] Daniel: Some; the mixed sequence lengths cause padding inefficiency. Continuous batching helps by grouping similar lengths together if the window is tuned, but it's not perfect. We suggested a small pre-classifier to separate short vs long requests before batching.
[03:40] Priya: Hmm could our client add a hint header with expected token length? That would help.
[03:45] Marcus: We can add a hint header, yes. We'll prototype in the test harness.
[03:50] Daniel: Great — that plus a two-lane setup should reduce p99s a lot.
[03:55] [04:00] Avery: Walk me through the queueing behavior we observed — you mentioned timeouts at ingress?
[04:06] Daniel: The ingress queue has a default transport-level timeout that retries by the client. When queue depth builds because of a sudden spike, some requests hit that timeout and then the client retries immediately, producing a retry storm. We saw cases where retries doubled QPS for a short stretch.
[04:20] Priya: Did Redwood's SDK retry backoff logic cause any of that?
[04:24] Daniel: No, the retries were at the app layer in the customer's test harness. We recommend exponential backoff and jitter on retries, and raising ingress queue capacity for bursts.
[04:34] Marcus: We'll update harness and add jitter.
[04:37] [04:40] Daniel: We also instrumented the GPU kernels and saw occasional SASS-level stalls when very large attention sizes happen; that's rare but contributes to long tails.
[04:50] Kendra: Any immediate mitigations?
[04:52] Daniel: On short term — pin min replicas to avoid cold adds, use two-lane routing for long seq, add pre-classifier or hint header, and tweak continuous_batching.window_ms to 14–20 depending on payload distribution. Also set queue_depth to 96 for smaller batches to reduce head-of-line blocking and avoid huge single batches.
[05:14] Priya: What about retries — you said increase ingress timeout? Which value?
[05:18] Daniel: We recommend increasing ingress timeout to 3.5s for this workload and enforce client-side backoff. Right now some of your attempts used 1s timeouts.
[05:29] Ellen: Okay. Any cost impact numbers if we pin capacity vs letting autoscaler do work?
[05:33] Avery: Short answer: pinning increases baseline cost but reduces p99 risk and can lower retry-induced extra QPS which hurts bills. We'll send a delta model. For the 2-hour run we advise reserving 10% extra capacity.
[05:47] [06:00] Daniel: One more nuance — KV cache sharding. Currently cache is sharded per replica which is great for throughput but during scaling we lose warm keys. We can try a shared external Redis backing for KV for warm persistence, but that'll add ~3–7ms median. It's a tradeoff.
[06:18] Marcus: Hmm, 3–7ms median is acceptable if p99 improves.
[06:22] Daniel: Yep. We'll include both options in the perf spreadsheet.
[06:28] Priya: Can we see the raw histogram of latencies? The slide shows averages but we need full distribution.
[06:33] Daniel: Absolutely — we'll upload the histograms (per-request latency, per-token latency) to the shared folder.
[06:38] [06:40] Priya: Any surprises in the logs?
[06:42] Daniel: A small number of retries were due to serialization backpressure on the ingress CPU when big batches are being prepared; that suggests either moving batching into a dedicated batching pod or increasing CPU for the staging pod.
[06:54] Jon: Our SRE would prefer fewer moving parts; might be easier to bump staging CPU and monitor.
[07:00] Daniel: Agreed for now. We'll provide recommended pod resources.
[07:05] [07:10] Avery: Let's talk concrete targets — what concurrency and batch settings should we aim for in the 2-hour run?
[07:15] Daniel: For the mixed profile I'd propose two lanes: lane A (short requests): max_concurrency 40, batch_window_ms 12, max_batch_tokens 8k, queue_depth 64. Lane B (long requests): max_concurrency 8, batch_window_ms 22, max_batch_tokens 64k, queue_depth 32. Route by hint header or payload size.
[07:40] Priya: Sounds reasonable. Will routing software be provided?
[07:44] Daniel: We'll share a sample Envoy config and a Redwood routing rule JSON. Marcus can drop it into the test harness.
[07:51] Marcus: Good.
[07:54] [08:00] Daniel: Expected outcome — short lane achieves <120ms p95 and p99 ~300ms; long lane p95 ~250–400ms and p99 ~800ms. Overall throughput should hit ~2.6k tok/s on two GPUs if the batching shapes align.
[08:17] Ellen: That's a big improvement if realized.
[08:20] Daniel: Yes but depends on batching shape and retries.
[08:23] Priya: What's the plan for warmup? Do you need pre-warm requests?
[08:27] Daniel: Yes — we recommend a 10–15 minute warmup phase where we send representative prefixes to populate the KV cache to avoid the early p99s. We'll include a warmup script in the runbook.
[08:38] [08:40] Avery: Anything on model variants or quantization we should consider?
[08:44] Daniel: For this pilot we stayed on the fp16 variant. Quantization to int8 showed minor token latency improvements but increased decode noise; we can test a quantized variant in parallel but don't swap in production without evals.
[08:58] Priya: Understood. We'll keep quantized as experimental.
[09:02] Kendra: Quick question from CS — what docs will you send after today's call?
[09:06] Avery: Perf spreadsheet, runbook with warmup script, suggested Envoy routing snippet, and the JSON for batching/concurrency. Also cost delta.
[09:13] Priya: When can we expect those?
[09:16] Avery: We'll push them by EOD 2025-12-03.
[09:20] [09:20] Marcus: I'll try to have the traffic profile by Friday so you can tailor the run.
[09:25] Daniel: Great — once we have that we'll run the 2-hour stress window early next week, preferably when you can monitor.
[09:33] Priya: We can do Tuesday morning.
[09:36] Avery: We'll tentatively schedule Tuesday 08:00 PT for the stress run.
[09:41] [09:45] Ellen: On the topic of monitoring, can Redwood stream per-token burn and per-request traces to our datadog?
[09:51] Daniel: Yes we have a tracing hook, we'll send the integration steps. There's a small sampling overhead but it's worth it.
[09:58] Jon: We'll enable low-sample tracing for the run.
[10:02] [10:10] Priya: Anything else before we wrap?
[10:13] Daniel: One last note — we observed some long GC pauses on the staging batching container that aligned with the larger sequences; increasing the JVM flags or bumping container memory helps. (transcription: container looked like JVM GC; could be another runtime in the path)
[10:30] Marcus: We'll check current container memory.
[10:33] [10:40] Avery: Alright recap — Daniel uploads logs & histograms, Avery shares perf spreadsheet + cost delta, Redwood shares runbook + Envoy snippet, customer provides traffic profile and will enable hint header in harness, schedule 2-hour stress run Tuesday 08:00 PT, follow-up meeting to review results.
[10:58] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward to the run.
[11:02] Avery: Thanks everyone.
